newsitem.title: USA: Most US stock index futures end choppy day higher.
newsitem.headline: Most US stock index futures end choppy day higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished mostly higher after a choppy session spent on both sides of Wednesday's close.
"It looks like no one wants to hold on to a position more than a nanosecond," a Standard and Poor's 500 futures trader said.
September S&P 500 futures posted an inside day on daily bar charts, a sign of market consolidation, traders said.
A slim lineup of significant data so far this week has left most stock indices at the mercy of technical factors and local interest, with trade called directionless today.

"It was like a day-trader session," another S&P 500 futures trader said. He said there was scant conviction on either side of the market, and drifting Treasury bonds did little to give the market direction.
September T-bonds closed down 1/32 at 113-28/32. September S&P 500s closed up 3.50 points at 921.50 in a range from 911.00 to 924.80.
September has failed to seriously retest the record high set Monday at 932.25, whipsawing all week instead. Support now rests at Wednesday's 906.50 session low and resistance at the record high.
Further upside targets were pegged at 935.00 and 937.50.
The economic lineup this week has been rather slim, and traders said they were looking to Friday morning's June producer price report.
The June producer price index was forecast unchanged overall and up 0.1 percent excluding food and energy. In the previous report, both readings fell 0.3 percent.
Before the open Thursday, the latest weekly jobless claims were reported up to 377,000 in the July 5 week from 337,000 the previous week.

At the close, September S&P 500s were up 3.50 points at 921.50, Nasdaq 100s fell 0.25 to 1021.25, Russell 2000s were up 3.30 points to 403.40, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 150.0 to 19,790.0 and Midcap 400s rose 2.80 points to 299.70.
